articles.title: Manappuram Finance shares drop 3% even as Q2 net profit soars 3x to Rs 701 crore. Why did Jefferies cut target price?
articles.summary: Shares of Manappuram Finance dropped around 3% on Friday after the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 701 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, surging over 3 times from Rs 220 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.The gold loan provider’s revenue from operations jumped 48% year-on-year to Rs 3,362 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 2,274 crore reported in the same period last year. The company’s total expenses jumped more than 23% YoY to Rs 2,434 crore, from Rs 1,973 crore reported in the year-ago period. Manappuram Finance’s gold loan and other segment recorded around 54% YoY rise in revenue to Rs 3,043 crore, while that for micro finance rose over 12% YoY to Rs 329 crore. The company’s standalone assets under management expanded 69% year-on-year to Rs 63733 crore at the end of September. The shares of the company dropped to Rs 311 apiece on NSE on Friday morning.Also read | Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit soars 77% YoY, but NPAs riseJefferies on Manappuram Finance share priceJefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Manappuram Finance shares but reduced its target price to Rs 400 apiece from Rs 430. The latest target price implies 25% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 320 apiece on NSE.The international brokerage noted that the company’s Q2 profit was 5% ahead of its estimates as higher net interest income offset higher provisions. It expects branch expansion and customer growth to drive 23% gold loan growth and 18% consolidated AUM growth in FY27. The company’s NIM rose 63 basis points sequentially to 11%, while gold loan yields rose 30 basis points QoQ to 18%, likely driven by customers slipping into higher-yielding (lower-rebate) slabs with longer repayment cycles, as per the rebate pricing structure, as well as penalty charges. Mannapuram Finance plans to price its loans competitively, but expects gold loan yields to sustain at 17.5-18%.However, the company saw some stress in shorter tenure schemes like peers. Its management indicated incremental trends are better as customers adapt, although the company is gradually shifting to longer tenure schemes.Also read | Manappuram Finance's Stage 2 gold loans jump tenfold to 5%Jefferies raised FY27-28 EPS estimates by 3-4%, factoring in lower AUM growth, better NIMs, lower opex & higher credit costs. articles.title: MSTC shares skyrocket 20% to hit upper circuit. Here’s why
articles.summary: MSTC shares surged 20% to hit the upper circuit at Rs 783.65 on the BSE after the state-owned e-commerce company reported its strongest second quarter since listing and received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India to operate a Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS).Consolidated profit before tax jumped 54.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 99.85 crore in the September quarter, while profit after tax rose 57.7% to Rs 74.92 crore. The company said both were its highest-ever Q2 figures since its listing in March 2019.Also Read | Ola Electric shares sink 6% as Q2 revenue falls 39% YoY. What's next?Revenue from operations increased 29.4% to Rs 110.02 crore, while total income rose 36.1% to Rs 139.21 crore. Standalone profit before tax climbed 50.5% to Rs 99.54 crore, while standalone profit after tax increased 51.8% to Rs 74.61 crore.The earnings growth was supported by a sharp increase in e-commerce activity. MSTC facilitated the sale of residential and multipurpose land parcels in Hyderabad, valued at Rs 2,863 crore, on behalf of the Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation and the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority.The company also partnered with the Karnataka Excise Department for the e-auction of liquor shop licences. The first tranche covered 125 licences and fetched around Rs 125 crore for the state government.Also Read | Jensen Huang forfeits $108 million in unvested Nvidia equityOther transactions during the quarter included the sale of an ONGC oil rig for $5.8 million, the first coal gasification event on behalf of the Ministry of Coal, and auctions of mineral and coal assets.MSTC also launched the eighth tranche of critical mineral block auctions, involving 13 new blocks and seven previously offered blocks. It sold around 400,000 tonnes of chrome valued at about Rs 718 crore and 1.54 million tonnes of coal valued at Rs 175 crore.The company’s e-commerce vertical remains its core growth driver. MSTC’s presentation showed that the platform crossed Rs 545.80 billion in transaction value during the first half of FY27, although the company has exited its legacy trading business.Another trigger for the stock was the RBI’s in-principle authorisation, received on November 11, to set up and operate a Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act. The board has directed the management to take the necessary steps to comply with the conditions attached to the approval.MSTC said it is developing the TReDS platform and is also examining the feasibility of setting up coal and other mineral exchanges. Its B2B travel portal is ready and is being upgraded for B2C operations.The Q2 performance marks a sharp improvement in profitability, with income growth significantly outpacing the rise in expenses. articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. Jones, who has been appointed Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board, said Kress has helped lead the company through a period of “extraordinary growth” and has a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.The board said it has “full confidence” in Kress and the leadership team and expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said.She added that Nvidia would continue advancing its work in accelerated computing and AI while focusing on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.Also Read | Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy honeytrap: How does China allegedly use this strategy to gather sensitive US information?Jensen Huang's Nvidia legacyThe board said Huang's contributions to Nvidia were “profound” and described the company as one of the world's most consequential technology companies.“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.Huang founded Nvidia and has led the company for 33 years, overseeing its transformation into a dominant player in accelerated computing and AI.A private affair, a very public exitHuang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been at the helm of the company for more than three decades. During that time, he transformed Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence boom. His departure marks a major change for the company and the semiconductor industry.Huang's exit comes amid a controversy involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. Huang admitted to having an extramarital relationship with her and apologised to his wife, children and Nvidia employees.The revelations prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company, however, said its board had no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. The affair finally cost Huang to step down from his position from the company.

articles.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
articles.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress and senior data-centre executive Ian Buck have been mentioned in discussions about possible leadership arrangements, but no successor has been announced.Nvidia is scheduled to report its quarterly results on November 17.Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on November 11, gaining 2.87% during the regular session. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. The company's market value had declined by roughly $600 billion since the board announced its investigation into the Alice Huang matter, according to the report.

articles.title: India’s Russian fossil fuel imports hit record
articles.summary: India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October, purchasing hydrocarbons worth €6.4 billion, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It was India’s highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022.Crude oil accounted for 91% of India’s purchases at €5.8 billion. Coal imports were worth €333 million, while oil products accounted for €232 million.Indian refineries raise Russian crude purchasesIndia’s imports of Russian crude oil rose 10% from September. Imports increased at all three of the country’s largest importing refineries—Vadinar, Jamnagar and Paradip.Imports at Vadinar rose 12% month-on-month, while Jamnagar and Paradip recorded increases of 22% and 28%, respectively. The rise made Jamnagar the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude in October.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei that use Russian crude exported oil products worth €1.6 billion to countries imposing sanctions in October. The destinations included the European Union, Australia, the US and New Zealand.Ten of the 12 shipments of oil products from refineries processing Russian crude that reached EU ports in October departed from India’s Jamnagar refinery. The remaining two shipments came from Turkiye’s STAR refinery.CREA estimated that €389 million worth of the oil products exported by these refineries were made from Russian crude. Exports from the refineries to sanctioning countries rose 21% in volume terms from September.Russia’s fossil fuel earnings reach four-year highChina remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, purchasing €10.7 billion worth of hydrocarbons in October. The European Union was the third-largest buyer at €2.2 billion, followed by Turkiye at €1.1 billion and South Korea at €488 million.Russia’s total fossil fuel export revenues rose 14% month-on-month to €754 million per day in October, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Export volumes remained broadly unchanged.Crude oil export revenues rose 19% to €449 million per day, with seaborne crude earnings increasing 23% to €352 million per day. CREA said this was the highest monthly level recorded since its data series began in January 2022.The report said higher global oil prices, linked to the energy crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, helped increase Russia’s fossil fuel earnings. Russia’s Urals crude averaged $101.70 a barrel in October, more than twice the EU and UK price cap of $44.10 a barrel.CREA also said that 60% of Russia’s seaborne oil was transported by sanctioned “shadow” tankers in October. Another 37% was carried by tankers owned or insured in G7 countries and their partners.A crude oil price cap of $30 a barrel, if fully enforced, would have reduced Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues by 21%, or €2.2 billion, in October, CREA said. A lower cap on crude and oil products together could have reduced Russia’s total seaborne oil export revenues by 25%, or €3.4 billion.

articles.title: US stock market selloff: Four indicators suggest correction may not be over
articles.summary: The recent selloff in US stocks has left investors searching for signs of a market bottom, but four key indicators suggest it may be too early to declare the correction over, according to a Reuters analysis.Technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks have fallen around 10% from their recent peaks after the Nasdaq-100 hit a record high in early October. While shares have stabilised somewhat, investor positioning, options activity and technical indicators continue to signal caution.Read more: Chinese yuan edges higher, but stronger dollar caps gains Technology positioning shows signs of easingAccording to Deutsche Bank data cited by Reuters, investors have reduced exposure to technology stocks since late September, shifting towards other sectors. The latest selloff pushed tech positioning below levels recorded during the April 2025 tariff-related market turmoil.Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte said the decline appeared to be driven by investors unwinding crowded positions. He added that positioning levels could create conditions for a technology sector rebound.Stock correlations offer some reliefAnother relatively positive signal is the limited increase in expected stock correlations. Barclays strategists noted that three-month realised correlation among the 50 largest S&P 500 companies fell to a record low in late September.Although expectations for correlations increased during last week's selloff, the rise remained modest. Rocky Fishman, founder of Asym Research, said this suggested investors viewed the decline as a sector-specific correction rather than a broader economic downturn, Reuters reported.Read more: South Korean shares rise as tech stocks rebound on Wall StreetOptions activity presents a mixed pictureRetail investors had purchased call options on individual stocks in record volumes this year, helping support the AI rally. However, that trend reversed sharply last week.According to Carrick Lane data, retail call buying in AI stocks dropped significantly, contributing to the post-election selloff.The shift has reduced excessive bullish positioning, but options indicators have not weakened enough to provide a strong buying signal.Technical indicators remain cautiousTechnical signals continue to suggest that the market may not have reached its bottom. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors, said the rebound in the Invesco QQQ ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, had stalled below its downward trend line.Weak short-term momentum and the absence of a DeMark exhaustion signal suggest US stocks could remain volatile for another couple of weeks, Newton said.Overall, while reduced technology exposure and relatively stable stock correlations offer some encouragement, options positioning and technical trends suggest investors should remain cautious before calling an end to the market correction.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)
